title: The four arrangements Jones wrote, Gerald Wilson's tune and Duke's last-minute habit
summary: Jones wrote four pieces on the album; they discuss Gerald Wilson's tune credited to Duke and Duke's last-minute pressure.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: You did all the writing on 'Ella at Duke's Place?'

No. Okay, he used 'Passion Flower,' which was Strayhorn's. It was already there. She sang it. She was able to sing it in the key that Johnny Hodges played it in. And then Duke did, 'Azure,' and I did, 'Calico Gown.' There was four things I did. I didn't do but four.
Wasn't that the session where Gerald Wilson brought in a number and Duke stole it from him?
Yeah, Gerald brought in a tune, that's right.

And Duke put his name on it? Changed one note in the melody and put his name on it as the composer and I think Gerald got co-composer or arranger credit. I think Gerald just got arranger credit. It was Gerald's tune.
I know, because Johnny Hodges played a solo on it, if I can remember right. Yeah, I remember that.

I remember I was amazed at Gerald's attitude, because I said, 'Gerald, didn't that bother you?' 'That was your tune, right?' And he said, 'Well, Duke changed one note in the melody.' And I said, 'But it was your tune.
Doesn't that bother you?" "Not really," he says. "Duke Ellington has given us so much that if I can give something to Duke Ellington it's my pleasure."
Well, all right, now, that's, yeah, that's quite an attitude.
Yeah, when it was his tune.

Yeah. Yeah. So -- I forget what else I did. But I did quite a bit of writing. And it was so funny, Norman Granz's secretary, Mary Jane Hopwater, said she thought that Duke really wanted me to do the whole album. I said, "Not at the last minute. Gee whiz."
That's the only way Duke did things, at the last minute.
Yeah. I said, "No, I can't." Oh, he thinks about it -- he thinks about it way up front.
He puts the pressure onto other people.
I mean everything had to be done yesterday.
